answer_1.quote: evaluate them on the following sequence-to-sequence tasks, reframed as text generation tasks without the requirement for task-specific fine-tuning: text summarisation, text simplification, and grammatical error correction (GEC).
answer_1.outputs: Generated text for summarization, simplification, and grammatical error correction

answer_2.quote: We used the most widely adopted reference-based metrics for each of the tasks. For text simplification, we report the SARI score. For text summarisation, we report the ROUGE score; following , we compute the geometric mean of ROUGE-{1, 2, L} F1 scores. For GEC, we report the F 0.5 score computed using the ERRANT toolkit.

answer_3.quote: We used GPT-4 as an additional reviewer to assess whether it can be reliably deployed in place of human reviewers.

answer_4.quote: Due to budgetary and time constraints, we recruited 3 human reviewers through the Prolific platform and asked them to review the quality of the models' outputs, as well as the gold reference on 100 randomly selected samples per dataset.
answer_4.guideline: Relevance, Fluency, Coherence, Consistency for summarization; Semantics, Fluency, Simplicity for simplification; Semantics, Grammaticality, Over-correction for GEC
